s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive gluteal swelling with mild erythema
salient_findings: 1-year history of slow but progressive swelling near the gluteal cleft
4 × 4 cm area of swelling with mild blanching erythema
No fluid obtained on percutaneous aspiration
Complex and septated 6 × 4 × 4 cm mass excised from subcutaneous tissue
key_facts: Swelling located near the gluteal cleft
No fevers, chills, pain, drainage, bleeding, or rectal bleeding
Mild blanching erythema of the overlying skin
No fluctuance, purulence, or visible pilonidal pits
Percutaneous aspiration performed with no fluid obtained
Surgical excision of a 6 × 4 × 4 cm mass
Mass was complex and septated, adherent to subcutaneous fat

shortlist.label: Epidermoid cyst
shortlist.why_kept: Clinical presentation of a slow-growing, painless mass near the gluteal cleft is consistent with an epidermoid cyst

shortlist.label: Dermoid cyst
shortlist.why_kept: Similar to epidermoid cyst, dermoid cysts can present as slow-growing, painless masses and are a plausible diagnosis given the location and characteristics of the mass

shortlist.label: Pilomatricoma
shortlist.why_kept: Pilomatricoma is a type of skin tumor that can present as a slow-growing, painless mass, and its location near the gluteal cleft makes it a possible diagnosis

shortlist.label: Lipoma
shortlist.why_kept: Lipoma is a common type of benign tumor that can occur in the subcutaneous tissue, and the description of the mass as a complex and septated lesion adherent to subcutaneous fat makes it a possible diagnosis

shortlist.label: Teratoma
shortlist.why_kept: Teratoma is a type of tumor that can contain multiple types of tissue, including skin, hair, and fat, and its location near the gluteal cleft makes it a possible diagnosis, although less likely than the other options

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of a slow-growing, painless swelling near the gluteal cleft, along with the surgical findings of a complex and septated mass in the subcutaneous tissue, is most consistent with an epidermoid cyst. The lack of fluid on percutaneous aspiration and the absence of fluctuance or purulence also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Dermoid cyst
rejected.why: Dermoid cysts often contain hair, teeth, or other tissue, which was not mentioned in the case

rejected.label: Pilomatricoma
rejected.why: Pilomatricomas are typically found on the head or neck and are less common in the gluteal region

rejected.label: Lipoma
rejected.why: Lipomas are usually soft and mobile, whereas the mass in this case was complex and septated

rejected.label: Teratoma
rejected.why: Teratomas often contain multiple types of tissue and can be more aggressive, which is not consistent with the patient's slow-growing and painless swelling
